title: The Cold War at its peak: January 1960
oneLine: Two nuclear superpowers face off over Berlin, empires are breaking up across Africa and Asia, and a new revolutionary government in Cuba sits 150 km from Florida.

whoIsWho.stance: Contain communism everywhere but avoid war; his second term ends in a year.
Wants the West out of Berlin and boasts of Soviet missiles, yet seeks a summit.
Drifting away from Moscow; his Great Leap Forward is causing famine at home.
Fighting in Algeria and building a French bomb to stay independent of Washington.
Seizing US-owned land and opening trade talks with Moscow.
Speaks for the new nations that refuse to pick a side.

whyItMatters: Both superpowers can already destroy each other's cities with nuclear weapons, and Berlin, Cuba and the Taiwan Strait are places where a local quarrel could drag them into war. Meanwhile dozens of newly independent countries are choosing sides, or refusing to.

timeline.text: Atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki; the Second World War ends.
NATO is founded, the Soviets test a bomb and Mao wins China's civil war.
North Korea invades the South; the Korean War ends in a 1953 armistice.
The Soviet Union and its allies form the Warsaw Pact.
The Soviet Union launches Sputnik, the first satellite.
Khrushchev demands that Western troops leave Berlin within six months.
Fidel Castro's rebels take power in Cuba.
